findings.problem: status is pub String instead of a domain enum. Any string value (e.g. "", "sent", "pending_sent", "DEAD") is representable, violating the core Holzman rule that illegal states must be unrepresentable.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any arbitrary string, making it impossible for the compiler to enforce valid lifecycle transitions. Downstream logic checking status via string comparison is both error-prone and bypasses compile-time guarantees.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a `pub status: SessionStatus` enum using the `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute. Remove the public setter and expose transitions only through typed methods or constructors.

findings.problem: is_validated is a pub bool lifecycle flag. Combined with is_sent and status (all pub fields), the struct allows arbitrary combinations like is_validated=false, is_sent=true, status="" simultaneously.
findings.failure_mode: No invariant enforcement: a session can be marked sent without being validated, or validated multiple times, or sent and then unsent. The three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent) encode overlapping state with no coordination, so illegal state combinations are trivially constructable.
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` with a single `SessionPhase` typestate enum that encodes the full lifecycle (e.g. `Created`, `Validated`, `Sent`). Make SessionWorkflow own the phase as a private field with typed accessors.

findings.problem: is_sent is a pub bool lifecycle flag. Redundant with status="sent" and is_validated, creating triple representation of the same lifecycle concept.
findings.failure_mode: Three separate fields encode overlapping lifecycle information with no mutual consistency check. The struct can be in an internally inconsistent state (e.g. is_sent=true but status!="sent"), making all downstream logic unsound.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool` entirely. Replace it with a typestate enum that makes the sent state a compiler-enforced variant. Access sent-ness via `matches!(phase, SessionPhase::Sent)` instead of a boolean field.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes SessionWorkflow by value and unconditionally mutates status and is_sent without any validation or typestate enforcement. There is no precondition check that the session was validated before sending.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can mark any session as sent regardless of validation state. The function performs a blind mutation with no guards, so invalid transitions (e.g. unvalidated -> sent) are accepted. This violates the functional-core imperative-shell boundary where the core should be pure and the shell should enforce invariants.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a typed state (e.g. `ValidatedSession`) as input and return a typed output (e.g. `SentSession`), making invalid transitions unrepresentable at the type level. Alternatively, return a Result<SessionWorkflow, TransitionError> and validate the current phase before mutating.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via `.to_string()` inside the core workflow logic instead of keeping the pure core inert and pushing mutation to the imperative shell.
findings.failure_mode: The core module performs string allocation (heap allocation) for what should be a pure state transition. This mixes side effects into the core and prevents the data layer from being truly inert and deterministic.
findings.fix: Push the allocation to the shell layer. The core should operate on immutable data or typed enum variants. Use `SessionStatus::Sent` enum variant instead of string comparison, eliminating the `.to_string()` call in the pure core.

findings.problem: All fields of SessionWorkflow are pub, exposing internal state for direct mutation by any caller.
findings.failure_mode: Any crate consumer can directly mutate `status`, `is_validated`, or `is_sent` without going through any validation or transition logic. This bypasses all lifecycle invariants and makes the struct's internal state externally mutable.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (`id` can be `pub` if it is read-only). Provide immutable accessors (`pub fn id(&self) -> &str`, `pub fn status(&self) -> SessionStatus`) and transition methods only.

findings.problem: id is a raw `String` with no domain-level newtype. There is no SessionId or SessionIdRef type to enforce that valid IDs are used where expected.
findings.failure_mode: Any string can be used as a session ID, including empty strings or malformed identifiers. This makes it impossible to distinguish valid session identifiers from garbage at compile time.
findings.fix: Introduce a `SessionId` newtype wrapping the internal representation (e.g. `pub struct SessionId(String)` with a fallible constructor, or use an existing domain ID type). Provide `SessionIdRef` for borrowed access.

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for the SessionWorkflow type and mark_sent function.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks or allocation tracking, there is no evidence that the performance characteristics of mark_sent (which allocates a String on every call) are acceptable for the workload. The `.to_string()` call on line 10 guarantees at least one heap allocation per transition.
findings.fix: Add a micro-benchmark for mark_sent measuring allocation count (via `allocations` or `criterion` allocation tracking), baseline against an enum-only approach, and report the command, number, and variance.

findings.problem: No `try_reserve` usage and no checked capacity arithmetic anywhere in the crate. The `.to_string()` call can unconditionally allocate without any allocation-failure handling.
findings.failure_mode: Under memory pressure, the unbounded allocation inside mark_sent can OOM the process instead of returning a typed Allocation error. This violates the Holzman requirement to handle allocation failure explicitly.
findings.fix: Either eliminate the allocation by using an enum for status (preferred), or if allocation is required, pre-compute capacity with checked arithmetic, use `try_reserve` before the allocation, and map allocation failure to a typed Allocation error.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation characteristics
no profiler data for SessionWorkflow lifecycle transitions
no allocation audit showing try_reserve or checked capacity handling
no second-ring analysis (no fuzz, proptest, or property-based tests for state transitions)
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy not run)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental architectural violations: primitive obsession (String/bool for domain state), no typestate enforcement making all illegal states representable, and mark_sent performs unguarded blind mutation. These are not lint-level issues but domain-model failures requiring structural refactoring before any Holzman Rust compliance is achievable.
